candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record supports HLH (bone marrow hemophagocytosis, splenomegaly, high fever) and CNS involvement (aseptic meningitis with leptomeningeal enhancement, elevated CSF pressure and protein, seizures/loss of consciousness). However, the lymph node biopsy is pathognomonic for KFD: confluent necrosis with apoptotic bodies, abundant histiocytes (CD68+, MPO+), expanded CD3+ T-cell paracortex, and paucity of B cells — the hallmark of Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease. The reference diagnosis designates KFD as the primary entity with HLH and aseptic meningitis as complications. C001 inverts this hierarchy by naming HLH as the primary diagnosis and relegating CNS disease to a complication, while entirely omitting KFD.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: C001 captures the HLH component and CNS involvement but omits the primary underlying etiology of Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease (KFD), which is the defining diagnostic entity driving the composite reference diagnosis

case_quality_flags: Lymph node histopathology is pathognomonic for KFD and is the anchor for the reference diagnosis; candidates that ignore this finding cannot achieve complete equivalence
HLH secondary to KFD is a recognized but uncommon complication; the composite reference requires all three components (KFD + HLH + aseptic meningitis)
